## Problem

A provider 400 meaning "your input is too big" surfaces to the caller as
`LLMUnavailableError: the LLM provider call failed` — provider-outage semantics for a
deterministic, caller-fixable input problem. The caller cannot tell "retry later, the provider
is down" from "shrink your input, this will never succeed".

Observed (scripted `ModelHTTPError`, offline):

```
ModelHTTPError(400, "prompt is too long: 206826 tokens > 200000 maximum")
  -> LLMUnavailableError: the LLM provider call failed
```

## Why this is a defect, not a design gap

rebar **already computes the correct classification**. `run_failure.py:152` holds
`CHANGE_INPUT` with `retryable=False` at the moment it wraps the error — and then wraps it in a
type whose name and message assert the opposite. Only the *type* is wrong; no new measurement,
estimator, calibration, or classification work is required.

Confirmed adjacent behaviour, so the blast radius is understood: there is **no** transport retry
(400 is absent from `_RETRY_STATUSES`) and **no** fallback (`CHANGE_INPUT` is excluded), so
nothing today depends on this presenting as an outage. But plan-review's size ladder burns a
full failed round-trip per rung against an error it cannot recognise as terminal-for-this-input.

## Scope — deliberately narrow

This is a **type/message correction at an existing classification site**, not a new guard.

Explicitly OUT of scope: any pre-flight measurement of the outgoing request. That is the
shared-seam design change tracked by `undamaged-adolescent-sable` (`f79d-e364-5fdb-417d`), which
needs a token estimator and a calibration decision this ticket does not touch. This fix acts
only AFTER the provider has answered, so it is a **complement, not a substitute** — it cannot
satisfy that ticket's "before the provider call" requirement and does not claim to.

Also out of scope: widening which HTTP statuses are classified `CHANGE_INPUT`. Use the
classification already computed at the wrap site; do not add new ones.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A provider 400 already classified `CHANGE_INPUT` at the wrap site raises an error whose
      type and message identify it as a caller-fixable input problem, not a provider outage —
      verified by a test scripting such an error offline and asserting on the raised type
- [x] The raised type remains a subclass of `LLMError`, so the 13 existing broad handlers keep
      catching it — verified by a test asserting the subclass relationship
- [x] A genuine provider outage (a 5xx, or a transport failure) still raises
      `LLMUnavailableError` — verified by a test, so the change discriminates rather than
      relabelling everything
- [x] No change to `_RETRY_STATUSES` or to fallback eligibility — verified by a test pinning
      that a `CHANGE_INPUT` 400 is still neither retried nor failed over
